prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor yard corner enclosed by a white wall on the right (roughly 1.5 to 3 metres away), a grassy ground plane below (1 to 2 metres away), and dense bushes ahead and to the left (2 to 4 metres away). In frames 1 and 2, the camera wearer's own torso, feet, and gloved right hand holding shears are at the bottom within 0.3 to 0.8 metres, while a second person on the left is 1 to 1.5 metres away (about 0.5 to 1 metre to the wearer's left) holding a long branch that arches across the foreground within arm's reach of both people; in frame 3 the second person is fully visible in the left foreground at about 0.8 to 1.2 metres facing forward and right toward the bushes (looking away from the camera wearer), in frame 4 only their lower body and left arm remain in view on the left at 1 to 1.5 metres as the camera pans or turns right, and in frame 5 the camera wearer's bare left arm extends forward at 0.3 to 0.6 metres toward the branches while the second person is out of view on the bottom-left. The depth map clearly separates the overhanging foreground branch and leaves (about 0.8 to 1.5 metres away) from the cluttered background foliage and ground plane behind them, which blend together in the RGB image. However, the depth map is unreliable along thin twigs that disappear or merge into the background, on the white wall where depth gradients shift inconsistently between frames, and in the upper-left foliage of frames 1, 2, and 4 where nearer bushes are rendered pitch black as if at infinite distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates body parts labeled as 'person' against the unsegmented black background in all five frames, along with a large false 'surfboard' mask on the right wall in frame 5. In frame 1 it segments the camera wearer's lower torso and gloved right arm at the bottom (0.3 to 0.5 metres away) and the second person's extended arm on the bottom-left (about 1 metre away); in frame 2 it detects the second person's legs and left arm on the left (1 to 1.5 metres away, split into overlapping 'person' masks) while missing most of the wearer's body except a tiny fragment at the bottom-left of the wearer's torso; in frame 3 it captures the second person's torso, head, and limbs on the left (about 0.8 to 1.2 metres away, facing away and to the right with the branch within their arm's reach); in frame 4 it segments the second person's lower body and arm on the left (1 to 1.5 metres away) and a tiny sliver of the wearer's foot at the bottom; and in frame 5 it segments only the camera wearer's outstretched left arm and hand in the lower-left foreground (0.3 to 0.6 metres away, within arm's reach of the branches). The map makes it easy to track the exact pixel boundaries and partial-frame occlusions of the two people across the severe top-down and side-cropped egocentric viewpoints without visual distraction from the busy foliage. However, it is highly unreliable for scene layout and objects: it misses all branches, bushes, and handheld tools, fragments the second person into duplicate 'person' instances in frames 2 and 4, misses the camera wearer's torso and legs in frames 2 and 4, and misclassifies the curved white boundary wall on the right in frame 5 (1.5 to 2.5 metres away) as a 'surfboard'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 4, detects a partial yellow body skeleton for the second person in frame 3, and detects only a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer in frame 5. In frame 3, the yellow keypoints show the second person positioned on the left at roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres from the camera wearer, with head/facial keypoints oriented to the right and away from the camera wearer, an upright torso box (shoulders and hips), and a right arm extending forward and right within arm's reach of the branch. In frame 5, the magenta skeleton captures the camera wearer's outstretched left hand and spread fingers about 0.4 to 0.6 metres in front of the camera, angled palm-away toward the foliage just in front of it. The pose map explicitly provides the 2D joint articulation of the second person's torso and right arm in frame 3 and the individual finger joints of the wearer's hand in frame 5 more abstractly than the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence because severe egocentric cropping and top-down angles cause it to miss all body and hand poses in frames 1, 2, and 4, omit the second person's legs, left arm, and hands in frame 3, and miss the wearer's arm and the second person's partially visible limb in frame 5.
